featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
It has been more than twenty years since I first visited Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar with my family, and it continues to remain a special place for us in Borivali. It is one of those restaurants in Borivali that continues to feel like home because of its food and hospitality.

This time, we began our meal with a bowl of Chicken Manchow Soup. It was served hot, and I enjoyed how it had a bold, flavorful taste without being overpowering. For starters, we ordered Veg Seekh Kebab, Mutton Seekh Kebab, and Chicken Pahadi Tikka. The Veg Seekh Kebab was nice, cooked well, and had the perfect earthy flavour. The Mutton Seekh Kebab was outstanding. It had a silky texture, was well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the chutney. It was not chewy at all, and I really liked how smooth it felt with every bite. The Chicken Pahadi Tikka was equally good. The chicken was tender, juicy, and cooked with a light smokiness that made it enjoyable.

For the mains, I ordered Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka. The dal had a nice garlic tempering with the right amount of cumin, and together with the rice it felt wholesome and comforting. The Chicken Tikka Masala came with soft pieces of chicken in a thick gravy that had a good balance of spices. It went really well with the Tandoori Roti, which was crisp on the edges and soft in the middle. The Chicken Triple Schezwan Fried Rice was the last dish. It was mildly spiced, had a smoky taste from the wok, and the flavours were balanced in a way that made it enjoyable till the last bite.

As we were about to finish, we couldn’t resist ordering the Chicken Masala Lollipop, which has always been a family favorite. It was crispy, spicy, and coated beautifully with sauce. It was the highlight of the evening. The chicken inside was fresh and well-cooked, and every bite reminded me why I have loved this dish here for years.

The food at Silver Coin Family Restaurant and Bar is consistently good, and the staff make the experience even better. They are polite, attentive, and always welcoming. This restaurant is more of a family place, and the presence of a bar only adds to the variety without taking away from its warm atmosphere.

Ratings:
Quality - 4/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 4.2/5
Price - ₹5000 for 8 people

For more mouthwatering food content, don’t forget to follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

-Total bill was 1780.

Post meal review-

Dear owners

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Since we were craving seafood for dinner, I decided to visit Konkan Kinara with my family. The restaurant had a minimalistic setup. When we arrived around 10:45 PM on a Friday night, the place was almost empty, with just one other table occupied. Since this is a Konkani restaurant, going by the name, I assumed they specialized only in Konkani cuisine. But to my surprise, they also served North Indian and Chinese dishes.

To start our meal, we ordered Manchow Soup. Then, we tried Bombil Fry, which was disappointing. Since this is a Konkani restaurant, I expected the fish to be well-marinated, but it tasted bland. So, I had to ask them to take it away. They were kind enough to serve it again, and this time, the flavors were much better.

Next, we tried Veg Seekh Kebab, which had a nice earthy flavor. The Orange Mojito was fresh and had a unique orange flavor. Then, we ordered Masala Papad, Chicken Thali, Mutton Thali, and Veg Thali. The masala papad was crispy and flavorful. The thalis were wholesome, and I feel one thali is more than enough for one person. With every thali, you have the option to choose between Bhakri, Chapati, or Wade, which adds a nice customization to the meal.

I especially liked the Chicken Thali, which came with bhakri. The bhakri was so soft, and I could tell from the taste that it was freshly made. The Veg Thali was also sufficient and included a sweet dish. To end the meal, we ordered Caramel Custard, which was delicious and properly made.

The staff was polite, but at times, they seemed more focused on watching a cricket match rather than attending to guests. We had to call them multiple times for basic service, like refilling water or checking on our order. A little more attentiveness would have made the experience much better.

The restaurant seemed hygienic to me, and overall, it was a decent experience at Konkan Kinara. If you are in the mood for a meat thali or seafood, you may consider visiting this place.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Sizzling Spices in Dahisar with my friends this weekend, and it turned out to be a delightful experience for Asian food lovers. The place is small but cozy, with quick and humble service that makes you feel welcome.

We began with the Chicken Eight Treasure Soup, which was packed with a variety of vegetables along with chicken – light, healthy, and a good start. Next came the Korean-style Crispy Chicken, essentially chicken katsu paired with honey chilli sauce. While the sauce was average, the katsu itself was perfectly crispy and enjoyable.

The highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the Chicken Thai Green Curry Pot Rice. Aromatic, rich in flavor, and served in a portion easily sufficient for three, it stood out as the star dish.

Overall, Sizzling Spices is a nice spot if you’re in the mood for hearty and flavorful Asian cuisine. Definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently placed an order from Sizzling Spices, and the highlight of my meal was undeniably the Chicken Thai Pot Rice. This dish is a true testament to the restaurant's dedication to delivering authentic Thai flavors in a sizzling and satisfying way.
The presentation of the Chicken Thai Pot Rice was visually appealing, served in a sizzling hot pot. The aroma alone was enough to make my mouth water. The dish featured tender pieces of chicken, perfectly cooked and seasoned to perfection, accompanied by a generous serving of rice.
The Thai spices were expertly balanced, offering a delightful combination of sweet, sour, and spicy notes. Fresh herbs and vegetables added a refreshing crunch to each bite, while the fragrant lemongrass and coconut milk infused the dish with an authentic Thai essence.The portion size was generous, making it ideal for sharing or savoring as a satisfying meal. The sizzling pot kept the dish warm throughout the meal, ensuring that every bite was as enjoyable as the first.

Whether you choose to pair your meal with a premium wine from our curated cellar, a signature cocktail from our lively bar counter, or enjoy it amidst the ambient lighting of our relaxed family lounge, Royale Masterchef ensures an incomparable dining experience in Dahisar West, Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
“Four Years, Dozens of Visits — This Review Is Long Overdue”

This review comes with an apology — to the restaurant.
I should have written this after my first visit, four years ago. What followed instead were repeated visits, quiet trust, and the kind of consistency that makes you forget to review… because you stop evaluating and start relying.

Ambience ⭐⭐⭐⭐½ /5
Royale Masterchef strikes a rare balance — elegant without being intimidating. The warm wood-paneled interiors, comfortable seating, and calm lighting make it equally suitable for couples, families, and even large groups. Over the years, I’ve been here with parents, with friends, and just as a couple — and the space adapts effortlessly each time.

Service ⭐⭐⭐⭐½ /5
There’s free valet parking (a blessing in Dahisar), and over time the staff has come to recognise me — which naturally elevates my experience. That said, even without familiarity, the service has always been polite, professional, and patient. On weekends it gets busy, and food does take time — but that time shows up on the plate. Good food doesn’t need shortcuts.

Food ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ /5
This is why I keep coming back.
Consistency is their superpower.

My regular orders over the years say enough: Chicken Cheese Kebab, Chicken Reshmi Kebab, Southern Fried Chicken, Honey Mustard Chicken, Chicken Tikka Masala, Mutton Biryani, Hakka Noodles, Chilli Garlic Noodles, and the dangerously good Mud Cake with Vanilla Ice Cream. I’ve explored nearly 90% of the menu, and it’s expansive. One honest miss? Chicken Lollipop — skip it.

Everything else? Gourmet-level execution that never fluctuates.

Drinks ⭐⭐⭐⭐ /5
From classic pours to simple pairings, the drinks complement the food well. This was once a regular stop for a quiet drink with dinner — responsibly adjusted now that I drive.

Value ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ /5
In four years, pricing has increased only once — and that too felt like inflation control, not opportunism. The value has remained intact.

Final Thoughts
This is not a flashy place. It doesn’t chase trends.
It just delivers — every single time.

Would I return? ✔
I already do. Again and again.

Visited Malvani Pahunchar for dinner recently. Make sure to reach early as they don’t take reservations — it’s strictly first come, first serve, so waiting time can be expected. They have both AC and non-AC seating sections. In ac section they have sitting of 4 tables so I don't think any large group can accommodate in that non ac is horizontal siting so they can club and sit together.

They serve authentic Malvani cuisine, and their variety of thalis are the main attraction — Surmai, Prawns, Chicken, etc.

We tried the Surmai Thali which included fish fry, sukkat, fish gravy, solkadhi, chutney, fish rassa, rice, and an option of bread (bhakri, vade, or chapati). Overall it was good, though the rassa wasn’t very jhanjhanit/spicy.

Chicken lollipop was spicy and tasty, and the Kombdi Wade tasted quite authentic.

We also tried their new ice cream flavours — Puran Poli, Modak, Jackfruit, and Ratnagiri Hapus Mango. We went for the mango ice cream and it was really good.

Overall, a good dining experience for authentic Malvani food lovers.

We recently tried a Malvani Pahunchar restaurant and ordered a chicken platter, chicken dish, prawns, and a bombil thali — and it turned out to be a proper coastal feast.
The chicken platter was generous and full of bold Malvani flavors. The spices were rich without overpowering the natural taste, and every bite had that smoky, masala-coated goodness. The chicken dish itself was cooked beautifully — tender, juicy, and soaked in a thick, aromatic gravy that paired perfectly with bhakri.
The prawns were the highlight for seafood lovers. Fresh, succulent, and cooked just right, they carried that authentic coastal spice blend that hits you with warmth rather than heat. And the bombil thali felt like a complete experience — crispy bombil, flavorful curry, and comforting sides that balanced everything out.
Overall, the meal felt homely yet indulgent — exactly what you hope for when craving Malvani cuisine. If you enjoy bold spices, fresh seafood, and hearty portions, this place definitely delivers.
